literal: He who knows the intention by looking, without speaking, is at all times an ornament to the world of unchanging water.
translation: One who can read another's mind simply by looking, without a word being spoken, is an ornament at all times to this world surrounded by the eternal sea.
modern: ஒருவர் வாயால் சொல்லாமலேயே அவருடைய முகத்தையும் கண்ணையும் நோக்கி அவரது குறிப்பை அறிந்துகொள்பவர், வற்றாத கடல் நீரால் சூழப்பட்ட இந்த உலகத்திற்கு எக்காலத்திலும் ஒரு சிறந்த அணிகலன் ஆவார்.
explanation: This couplet praises the rare and valuable skill of reading another person's mind or intentions without them having to express it in words. The poet states that a person who possesses this intuitive ability is a true ornament to the entire world. The world is described as being surrounded by 'unchanging water', referring to the vast, eternal ocean. By comparing such an insightful person to a precious jewel, the couplet highlights how highly society values those who can perceive unspoken thoughts and feelings through simple observation.
